claims.statement: Both synchronous and asynchronous eval handlers patch the enclosing ToolRuntime callback configuration, so PTC tool calls and task dispatches are child callback runs of the eval invocation rather than the agent tools step; this trace nesting does not restore parent ToolNode per-action interrupt_on or HITL enforcement.

QuickJS task dispatch emits custom-stream subagent start and complete or error events keyed by a dispatch ID derived from the parent eval ID and request payload; replay can reproduce the ID, telemetry writer failures do not break dispatch, and graph interruptions propagate.

QuickJS is agent-process middleware rather than a remote sandbox provider: CodeInterpreterMiddleware exposes an eval tool and private slot/snapshot state, while a lazy slot owns a worker, runtime, and REPL context; concurrent evaluations fail rather than queue.

QuickJS fs is disabled unless configured, and its asynchronous Node-style operations call the bound backend directly; they bypass FilesystemMiddleware, create_deep_agent permissions, and interrupt_on approval, so code receives all filesystem reach of that backend.

QuickJS thread persistence stores full snapshot bytes as a deterministic DeltaChannel anchor-or-bsdiff patch chain; an optional HMAC authenticates reconstructed bytes against the private slot ID, and invalid signatures or restore failures clear saved state without executing requested code.

QuickJS maintains a process-wide LRU of at most 32 warm slots; acquisition leases a slot, and capacity eviction closes only unleased slots with no running eval, so active evaluations are not terminated by registry eviction.

QuickJS PTC exposes only configured tools after upstream filtering, excludes eval itself, applies a per-eval bridge-call budget shared with fs, and invokes selected tools through the REPL bridge rather than the normal ToolNode path; disabling the budget permits unbounded host-call loops.
QuickJS 0.4.0 requires Python >=3.11,<4.0 and Deep Agents >=0.7.42,<0.8.0, and declares bounded dependencies on quickjs-rs, LangChain, LangChain Core, LangGraph, and bsdiff4.

The persistence mode controls context lifetime: thread mode snapshots state after an agent run, turn mode closes its context after the run without persisting, and call mode closes the context after each eval.

before_agent assigns or validates private slot state without allocating a VM, closes a stale context left by a non-resume run unless it matches the saved snapshot, and restoration occurs lazily on eval.

A QuickJS task bridge validates task input, finds the active Deep Agents task tool, and limits concurrent task dispatches with a per-REPL semaphore whose default is 32; it is not a process-wide or total-dispatch limit.

When the code-agent factory enables its interpreter, it installs CostAwareCodeInterpreterMiddleware as js_eval and rejects the in-process interpreter when a remote sandbox is configured; the subclass leaves synchronous tool execution unchanged and adds its receipt transport only on the asynchronous eval path.

For JavaScript-dispatched subagents, the code-agent adapter assigns isolated deterministic child checkpoint namespaces and an enclosing eval cost owner, persists each local cost receipt once, then the outer owner aggregates receipts into a parent-scope session-cost transfer; nested owners do not emit a second transfer.

The optional partner distributions currently publish distinct compatibility contracts: Daytona 0.0.9, Modal 0.0.8, Runloop 0.0.7, and Vercel Sandbox 0.0.2 all require Python >=3.11,<4.0 and Deep Agents >=0.7.42,<0.8.0, while their provider SDK requirements respectively are daytona>=0.197.0,<1, modal>=1.5.3, unbounded runloop-api-client, and vercel>=0.5.9.

deepagents-code declares QuickJS as a base dependency, exposes the Daytona, Modal, Runloop, and Vercel integrations as optional sandbox extras, and groups those remote-provider extras under all-sandboxes.

When deepagents-code receives a remote sandbox, it uses that object as the backend supplying file and execution tools instead of local shell middleware, and it rejects enable_interpreter=True rather than combining the in-process JavaScript interpreter with that remote-sandbox mode.

DaytonaSandbox isolates each command in a newly created Daytona session and deletes that session in finally; a bounded command deadline produces exit code 124, attempts partial-log recovery, and shares a two-second best-effort cleanup budget with session deletion.

RunloopProvider attaches to an explicit devbox ID or creates a new devbox, with blueprint selection ordered as RUNLOOP_SANDBOX_BLUEPRINT_ID, explicit snapshot name, then RUNLOOP_SANDBOX_BLUEPRINT_NAME; named blueprints are built only when missing and non-ready matches fail rather than being rebuilt.

VercelSandbox runs commands detached and locally waits for completion; on timeout it attempts to kill the provider command and returns exit code 124, while a completed-command log-fetch failure retains the exit code with an unavailable-output response and combined output is truncated at 100,000 characters.
